questions.prompt: When the enemy was drawing near, the weary soldiers cared for their bodies in the camp.
questions.answer: Hostibus appropinquantibus, mīlitēs fessī corpora in castrīs cūrābant.

questions.prompt: The victorious generals ordered the legions to return home.
questions.answer: Ducēs victōrēs legiōnēs domōs redīre iussērunt.

questions.prompt: Themistocles renewed the courage of the citizens by his own eloquence.
questions.answer: Themistoclēs ēloquentiā suā animōs cīvium recreāvit.

questions.prompt: When the city had been captured, everything was lost.
questions.answer: Urbe captā, omnia āmissa sunt.

questions.prompt: Since this is so, we must lay aside all hope.
questions.answer: Quae cum ita sint, omnem spem dēpōnere dēbēmus.

questions.prompt: These things are very well known to everyone in the province.
questions.answer: Haec omnibus in prōvinciā pervulgāta sunt.

questions.prompt: The commander announced that everything had been prepared for the journey.
questions.answer: Dux omnia ad iter parāta esse nūntiāvit.

questions.prompt: From boyhood he gave himself to the study of philosophy.
questions.answer: Ā puerō studiō philosophiae sē dēdidit.

questions.prompt: In Sulla's dictatorship many citizens were driven into exile.
questions.answer: Sullā dictātōre multī cīvēs in exsilium āctī sunt.

questions.prompt: Under my leadership the army swiftly crossed the river.
questions.answer: Mē duce exercitus flūmen citō trānsiit.

questions.prompt: Themistocles's foresight saved Greece from the barbarians.
questions.answer: Prūdentiā Themistoclīs Graecia ā barbarīs servāta est.

questions.prompt: Everything that had been promised was accomplished by the consul.
questions.answer: Omnia quae prōmissa erant ā cōnsule perfecta sunt.

questions.prompt: Since these things are true, we ought to trust the messenger.
questions.answer: Quae cum vēra sint, nūntiō crēdere dēbēmus.

questions.prompt: In Caesar's consulship the laws were changed.
questions.answer: Caesare cōnsule lēgēs mūtātae sunt.

questions.prompt: Under so great a leader the soldiers feared nothing.
questions.answer: Tantō duce mīlitēs nihil timēbant.

questions.prompt: The Germans, though wounded, cared for their bodies before the battle.
questions.answer: Germānī, quamquam vulnerātī, ante proelium corpora cūrāvērunt.

questions.prompt: With a brief speech the general renewed the courage of his soldiers.
questions.answer: Dux brevī ōrātiōne animōs mīlitum recreāvit.

questions.prompt: Under Caesar's leadership the soldiers guarded the bridge with great care.
questions.answer: Caesare duce mīlitēs pontem magnā cūrā custōdiēbant.

questions.prompt: When the ships had been burned, everything seemed lost to the allies.
questions.answer: Nāvibus incēnsīs, omnia sociīs perdita vidēbantur.

questions.prompt: Since this is so, we ought to abstain from war.
questions.answer: Quae cum ita sint, ā bellō abstinēre dēbēmus.

questions.prompt: By the foresight of the commander the city was saved from the flames.
questions.answer: Prūdentiā imperātōris urbs ex flammīs servāta est.

questions.prompt: In Sulla's dictatorship these things were well known to all.
questions.answer: Sullā dictātōre haec omnibus pervulgāta erant.

questions.prompt: From boyhood the poet loved learned books full of wisdom.
questions.answer: Ā puerō poēta librōs sapientiae plēnōs amābat.

questions.prompt: Under my leadership the citizens will care for their minds and bodies.
questions.answer: Mē duce cīvēs et animōs et corpora cūrābunt.

questions.prompt: By the counsel of Themistocles Greece was freed from great dangers.
questions.answer: Cōnsiliō Themistoclīs Graecia magnīs perīculīs līberāta est.
